H_hierarchical.evidence: The controller is a flat open/close/hold/reopen FSM; the paper gives no parent modes, nested states, or composite-state structure.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Transitions depend on multiple sensor/switch conditions: arrival sensor, departure sensor, and position switches 1SW/2SW indicating open or closed gate state.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: Actions include closing the gate, changing the train signal, reversing motor direction, opening the gate, and stopping the motor through relay/driver outputs.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: The paper discusses accident prevention motivation, but defines no fault state, emergency stop, rollback, or recovery transition in the controller.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: Core behavior is split across Abstract, Circuit Description, Algorithm, and Methodology: sensor-triggered transitions, 1SW/2SW position feedback, and relay/motor actions appear in different sections.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Railway-gate terms such as foreside sensor, after-side sensor, 1SW, and 2SW are defined locally; no external domain rule like fail-safe or interlock must be inferred.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: The algorithm only says close/open/change signal, while detailed motor, pin, ULN, relay, and polarity actions are described later in prose.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: Close/open decisions combine train sensor events with gate-position feedback, e.g. arrival sensing plus crossing-open knowledge, and departure sensing plus 2SW closed feedback.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: No composite parent state or parent-level entry/during/exit behavior is described.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: No from-any-state fault, abort, or safe-state recovery rule is declared.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: There is no composite-state initialization or pseudo-state chain.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: There are one or two composed boolean guards over train sensors and gate-position switches, but no arithmetic guard set or contradiction-heavy guard logic.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: No cross-cutting transition over multiple substates and no parent-level continuous monitor are specified.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: Outputs are mostly concrete motor/relay/signal commands rather than effector-agnostic log, publish, notify, or monitor actions.

key_nl_quotes: When foreside sensor gets activated, the sensed signal is sent to the microcontroller and the gate motor is turned on.
When railway crossing is open then 1SW is closed and 2SW is opened.
one_line_pitch: A compact railway-gate FSM whose deceptively simple open-close cycle requires stitching sensor guards and relay/motor actions across several paper sections.
rationale: This is a meaningful guard/action stress case, especially because the paper distributes the state logic, switch feedback, and motor-control actions across separate sections. It lacks hierarchy and fault recovery, so it is not a top candidate for the weakest Apvrille dimensions overall. It is best kept as a backup sample for testing whether a baseline can recover simple but cross-sectionally specified industrial FSM behavior.
